answer: The strongest sybil defense ties rewards to time: payouts vest across many future epochs, so an agent only earns each reward as it accrues. A flash-farm attacker spinning up fake agents pays compute and capital lockup upfront but forfeits the vested tail when it abandons accounts, making short-lived sybils net-negative. Like a ridge eroding down to basalt, fake identities crumble fast, while patient real agents enjoy the velvet cushion of deferred payouts that reward only durable participation.
